subject: Re: alternative method of incorporating model selection

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: alternative method of incorporating model selection
parts:
I think there is a conceptual difference between the two strategies. In
the first, you're allowing any of the possible models to be the 'true'
model, and you're quantifying the variation arising from using different
models supported by the data. With your proposed approach, you're
essentially saying that the 'true' model is an average of the selected
models, and you're using the bootstrap to quantify uncertainty arising
from having to estimate the weights. I would expect this approach to
yield smaller variances, and not really to quantify model uncertainty
appropriately.

Steve Buckland

Eric Stolen wrote:
> > I would like to get some input on the pros and cons of an alternative method
> > of incorporating model selection uncertainty into estimates of variance using
> > bootstrapping in a multiple covariate distance sampling analysis.
> >
> > Currently, model averaging is incorporated during the bootstrap option of
> > variance estimation. It works by fitting a set of up to 5 detection functions
> > to the bootstrap sample data at each iteration, and the top model being
> > selected and used for the abundance estimation for that iteration. Model
> > selection uncertainty is thereby included in the width of the ensuing
> > confidence intervals calculated from the bootstrap estimates.
> >
> > My alternative method differs by using a single set of best models, selected
> > from the original data, to compute a model-average estimate at each
> > iteration. In other words, I first use the original data to select a set of best
> > models to use for estimation. Then, at each iteration of the bootstrap I
> > compute the model average estimate of abundance based on this set of
> > models and associated parameter estimates. The model average estimate is
> > the average of estimates weighted by model weight. The bootstrap
> > abundance estimate and 95% confidence limits are then calculated as usual.
> >
> > An analyst might prefer this method for 2 reasons: 1) For some data (e.g.
> > sparse data) there will likely be convergence problems that will go undetected
> > in some (perhaps many) iterations during the automated model selection
> > occurring in each bootstrap iteration. 2) It is computationally challenging to
> > have to re-fit a set of detection functions at each iteration, especially when
> > covariates differ across models in multiple covariate distance sampling.
> >
> > The basic question is: "does my proposed method adequately incorporate
> > model selection uncertainty, given the constraints I mention?"
> >
